name: Document Parsing and OCR
question: Did the text, tables and layout survive ingestion?
summary: Turns PDFs, scans, slides and spreadsheets into clean text with its structure before anything is chunked or embedded. Digital pages give up their text layer; scanned pages need OCR, including Hindi and other Indian scripts; layout detection restores reading order across columns and drops running headers; tables are kept as rows with their headers; and page and section numbers travel with the text for citations. What is lost here cannot be retrieved later.
useCases: Scanned KYC forms, agreements and old circulars
Reports and statements full of tables
Multi-column documents such as regulations and research papers

items.detail: extract digital text directly; it is exact and fast
render scans at about 300 dpi; set the languages, such as eng + hin
Markdown or HTML rows that keep the header
document, page, section and date for citations and filters
empty pages, garbled characters, low OCR confidence

steps: Check each page for a text layer and OCR only the pages without one
Restore reading order and drop running headers and footers
Convert tables to Markdown with their header row
Keep page and section metadata, and send near-empty pages to review
pitfalls: Scanned pages ingested as blank text, silently
Tables flattened into a stream of numbers with no headers
Two-column pages read straight across both columns
remember: Parse for structure, not just text.
caption: Illustrative: Kosh Finance, a fictional NBFC, ingests 2,000 pages of loan files: digital, scanned, tabular and two-column.

steps.title: Check for a text layer
steps.text: Digital PDFs carry their text; extracting it is exact and takes milliseconds. A page with almost no extractable text is almost certainly a scan.

steps.title: OCR the scans, in the right languages
steps.text: Render the scanned page at 300 dpi and run OCR with English and Hindi models. Without “hin”, a Hindi KYC declaration comes back as noise.

steps.title: Restore the layout
steps.text: Drop the running header and footer bands, then read the left column before the right. Read straight across, a two-column circular mixes two paragraphs line by line.

steps.title: Keep tables as tables
steps.text: The interest-rate table becomes Markdown rows with a header: | Tenure | Rate |. Flattened, it is a stream of numbers no one can match to a question.

steps.title: Carry the metadata
steps.text: Every piece keeps its document, page and kind. Citations and filters later depend on it: “loan_2023.pdf, page 7”.

steps.title: Flag near-empty pages
steps.text: A page with under 200 characters goes to a review queue. Silent blanks are the most common ingestion bug.

pros: Recovers text from scans, tables and columns that naive extraction loses
Metadata such as page and section makes citations and filters possible
Quality checks catch silent failures before anyone asks a question
Fixes at ingestion help every question, for every model
cons: OCR and layout models add minutes per thousand pages
Hindi and regional scripts need the right OCR models and testing
Complex layouts still need human review
avoidWhen: Every document is clean digital text with no tables (plain text extraction is enough)
The documents are already structured data (load the database, do not parse exports)

practice.scenario: Kosh Finance, a fictional NBFC, indexes 2,000 pages of loan files for its credit team: agreements, sanction letters, statements and scanned KYC forms, some in Hindi. Digital pages give up their text directly; scans are OCRed in English and Hindi; tables become rows with headers; and every piece keeps its document and page so answers can cite them. Pages that come back nearly empty go to a review queue.

industries.use: Loan agreements, sanction letters and scanned KYC forms
Claim forms, hospital bills and discharge summaries, often photographed
Gazette notifications and judgments in several languages and layouts

practice.analogy: Unpacking a moving van. If you throw every box's contents into one pile, you will never find the cutlery; label each box and keep the drawers together.

library.name: Docling
library.what: Open-source document conversion from IBM: layout analysis, reading order, table structure and OCR, exporting clean Markdown or JSON with page provenance.

practice.note: OCR engines and language models vary by version; test on your own scans, including Hindi and low-quality photos.

samples.code:
from docling.document_converter import DocumentConverter

converter = DocumentConverter()                 # layout, tables and OCR built in
result = converter.convert("loan_agreement_2023.pdf")
doc = result.document

markdown = doc.export_to_markdown()             # headings, lists and tables as Markdown
for table in doc.tables:
    df = table.export_to_dataframe(doc=doc)     # keep tables as structured rows
    print(df.head())

for item, level in doc.iterate_items():         # every element keeps its provenance
    if item.prov:
        print(item.prov[0].page_no, item.label, str(getattr(item, "text", ""))[:60])

numericDrill.question: 500 of 2,000 pages are scans. OCR takes 1.5 seconds a page on one worker. With 5 workers in parallel, how many minutes does OCR take?
numericDrill.answer: 500 × 1.5 s = 750 s of OCR work; across 5 workers that is 150 s, or 2.5 minutes. OCR only the pages without a text layer, not all 2,000.

interview.question: How do you make sure scanned PDFs are actually searchable in a RAG system?
interview.answer: Detect pages without a text layer and OCR them at about 300 dpi with the right languages, such as English and Hindi. Check characters per page after parsing and send near-empty pages to review. Keep page numbers so answers can cite the page, and sample-check OCR quality on real documents.

interview.question: Why do tables cause so many RAG failures, and what do you do about them?
interview.answer: Naive extraction flattens tables into a stream of numbers, so values lose their row and column headers. Extract tables as Markdown or HTML rows with headers, never split a row across chunks, and add table questions to the evaluation set.

mistakes.mistake: Assuming every PDF has a text layer
mistakes.fix: Check each page and OCR the ones without text
Keep tables as rows with their headers

quiz.question: A loan PDF page returns 8 characters from its text layer. What is the most likely explanation?
options: The page is a scanned image and needs OCR
quiz.explanation: Scanned pages have no real text layer; a stamp or page number may be all that is extractable. Route such pages to OCR.

quiz.question: Claim forms arrive as phone photos in Hindi and English. Which OCR setting matters most?
options: Both languages enabled, for example eng+hin
Lower image resolution to save time
quiz.explanation: OCR only recognises scripts it has models for; without Hindi the Devanagari text becomes noise.

quiz.question: A rate table is extracted as “12 m 11.5% 24 m 12.0% 36 m 12.5%”. What is lost?
options: Which value belongs to which column header
quiz.explanation: Flattened tables lose their structure; keep them as rows with headers.

quiz.question: Which steps belong in a parsing pipeline for mixed PDFs? Select all that apply.
options: Detect pages without a text layer
Restore reading order on multi-column pages
Translate every page into English before indexing
quiz.explanation: Detection, OCR and layout are core. Translation is a separate choice and can hurt exact matching.

quiz.question: A two-column judgment is read straight across each line. What happens to retrieval?
options: It improves, because lines are longer
Sentences from both columns interleave, so chunks lose their meaning
quiz.explanation: Interleaved columns produce incoherent text that neither embeddings nor keywords handle well.

quiz.question: 500 pages need OCR at 1.5 seconds a page on 4 parallel workers. How long does OCR take?
quiz.explanation: 500 × 1.5 = 750 s of work; ÷ 4 workers ≈ 188 s, about 3 minutes.

quiz.question: Every chunk begins with “Vendor Terms · Confidential · Page n”. What is the effect?
options: Unrelated chunks look similar, adding noise to retrieval
quiz.explanation: Running headers repeat on every page and pull unrelated chunks together. Drop them during parsing.

quiz.question: Why keep the page number and section with each parsed piece?
options: So answers can cite the page and filters can use the section
quiz.explanation: Metadata enables citations, filters and debugging; it is not mainly for retrieval scores.

quiz.question: After parsing, 60 of 2,000 pages have under 200 characters. What should happen?
options: Review them: they may be failed OCR, photos or the wrong language
quiz.explanation: Near-empty pages are the most common silent ingestion failure.

quiz.question: Which tools can OCR or analyse the layout of scanned documents? Select all that apply.
quiz.explanation: BM25 is a ranking function, not a parser.

quiz.question: A contract PDF is digital, with tables. What is the cheapest correct approach?
options: Extract the text layer and use a table extractor
Screenshot each page for a vision model
quiz.explanation: Digital pages already carry exact text; OCR would only add errors and time.

quiz.question: Why is OCR rendered at about 300 dpi rather than 72 dpi?
options: Small characters need enough pixels to be recognised
quiz.explanation: Low resolution blurs small text; 300 dpi is a common default for OCR.

quiz.question: A scheme notice mixes Hindi and English on the same page. What is the best OCR setup?
options: OCR twice and keep the longer output
quiz.explanation: Mixed-language pages need both models at once.

quiz.question: Parsing changed, so tables are now extracted properly. What else must happen?
options: Re-chunk and re-embed the affected documents
quiz.explanation: New text means new chunks and new embeddings.

quiz.question: Test questions answered from tables fail at 65%, others at 10%. What should you inspect first?
options: How tables were parsed and chunked
quiz.explanation: The failure concentrates on one page type, which points to parsing.

quiz.question: Which are signs of a parsing problem rather than a retrieval problem? Select all that apply.
options: The answer text does not appear anywhere in the index
Tables appear as streams of numbers
The right chunk exists but ranks 20th
Two columns interleave in the chunk text
quiz.explanation: A chunk ranked 20th exists; that is a ranking problem.

quiz.question: A vision-language model can read page images directly. When is that worth it?
options: For complex visual pages such as charts or forms, where text extraction fails
quiz.explanation: Vision models are slower and costlier; use them where structure defeats ordinary parsing.

quiz.question: Headers are dropped by removing text in the top and bottom 50 points of each page. What is the risk?
options: A real heading or table near the edge may be lost; check on samples
quiz.explanation: Band-based rules are simple; verify them on real layouts.

quiz.question: What is the most useful measure of ingestion quality?
options: How many test questions have their answer text present in the index
quiz.explanation: Tie ingestion quality to answerable questions, not raw volume.

quiz.question: A scanned gazette page OCRs with many garbled characters. What could help?
options: A cleaner scan or preprocessing such as deskewing and binarisation
quiz.explanation: Image quality drives OCR quality; fix the input before the downstream steps.
